Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:10:1.english: Is as though [it were] collected - For he has mortgaged his lands to him for the principal and for the interest.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:10:2.hebrew: עבדו לאיסורייהו - וקריעתו הויא השבתו, ואם גבו נמי הוו מיחייבי ליה לאהדורי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:10:2.english: They performed their transgression - And tearing it up is its return, and if they had [actually] collected [it] as well, they would have been obligated to return it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:10:3.english: He has done nothing - And who disagrees with them?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:11:1.english: Actually, [it] is not as though collected - And it is for mere appraisal [that] the first Tanna holds him liable.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:12:1.hebrew: דתנן כו' - ואי אמרת לא מחייבי עד דגבו, בשלמא כולהו עבדי מעשה בגבייתו — מלוה גובה מן הערב, והערב מן הלוה, הלוה נתן ביד המלוה ועבר בלא תשיך (דברים כג) — אלא עדים מאי עבוד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:12:1.english: As we learned, etc. - And if you say [that] they do not become liable until they collect [the interest], granted, all of them perform an action at its collection — [the] lender collects from the guarantor, and the guarantor [collects] from the borrower, [and] the borrower placed [it] into the hand of the lender and transgressed [the prohibition of] "You shall not pay interest" (Deuteronomy 23) — but what [action] did the witnesses perform?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:12:2.english: Rather, is it not because of appraisal - Therefore, the lender and the guarantor are also liable from the outset because of [the] appraisal.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:13:1.english: By their laws - Of the nations, to whom interest was not forbidden.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:13:2.hebrew: מוציאין מן הלוה למלוה - אם אין לו משכון, ע"י שביניהם, כגון רבית קצוצה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:13:2.english: One removes from the borrower [to give] to the lender - If he does not have a pledge, [they extract it] by means of [the agreement] between them, such as fixed interest.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:13:3.hebrew: בדינינו - אם גבה, מחזירין לו כר' אלעזר. ולקמיה פריך ליה מאבק רבית, דבדיניהם מוציאין ובדינינו אין מחזירין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:13:3.english: By our laws - If he already collected [it], we return [it] to him, in accordance with Rabbi Elazar. And later on, [the Gemara] raises a difficulty against him from [the case of] indirect interest, where by their laws they extract [it], yet by our laws we do not return [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:13:4.english: Any [case] where by their laws they do not extract [it] - [The Gemara] explains [this] later.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:14:1.hebrew: ובדינינו אין מחזירין - את העודף ביוקר, שהוקירו החטים בשעת תשלומין, דהא אבק רבית הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:14:1.english: And by our laws one does not return - the excess [due to] the higher price, [in that] the wheat appreciated at the time of payment, for this is "dust of interest" [rabbinic interest].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:14:2.hebrew: אינהו בתורת פקדון אתו לידיה - אינהו כי מגבו סאה בסאה מן הלוה למלוה, לאו בתורת רבית קא מגבו ליה, אלא בתורת פקדון הוא בעיניהם, דהא סאה מסר לו בידו. וכי אמר רב ספרא למילתיה, הכי אמרה: כל שבדיניהם מוציאין בתורת רבית, בדינינו מחזירין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:14:2.english: [As for] them, it came into his hand as a deposit - When they collect a se'ah for a se'ah from the borrower for the lender, they do not collect it as interest; rather, it is [regarded] as a deposit in their eyes, for behold, he handed a se'ah into his hand. And when Rav Safra stated his dictum, he stated it thus: Whatever they extract by their laws as interest, by our laws we return [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:15:1.hebrew: משכנתא בלא נכייתא - מלוה מעות על הכרם ואוכל את הפירות, ואינו פוסק לנכות לו מן החוב כלום בשביל אכילתו, ואוכל בתורת רבית:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:15:1.english: A mortgage without deduction - [One] lends money on a vineyard and consumes the produce, and does not stipulate to deduct anything from the debt for him on account of his consumption, and [thus] consumes [it] as interest.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:15:2.english: That by their laws they extract - if the borrower consumed the produce after he mortgaged it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:1:1.hebrew: וחי אחיך עמך - רישיה דקרא ברבית קאי, אל תקח מאתו וגו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:1:1.english: And your brother shall live with you - The beginning of the verse refers to interest: "Do not take from him, etc."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:2:1.hebrew: אם ישתו שניהם ימותו - בצמא, שאין מספיק לשניהם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:2:1.english: If both of them drink, they will die - Of thirst, for [there is] not enough for both of them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:2:2.english: And if the one drinks, he will reach a settled area - And he will find water.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:2:3.english: With you - Your life takes precedence.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:3:1.hebrew: אינהו הוא דאין חייבין להחזיר - כדתרצה רבה בהגוזל בתרא (ב"ק דף קיב.), "וחי אחיך עמך" — לדידיה הוא דאזהריה רחמנא, אהדר ליה דניחי בהדך, דסיפיה דקרא ארישיה קאי: אל תקח, ואם לקחת החזר. אבל לבריה לא אזהר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:3:1.english: It is they who are not obligated to return [it] - As Rabbah resolved it in [the chapter] HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 112a): "[And] your brother shall live with you" — it is him whom the Merciful One warned: "Return [it] to him so that he may live with you," for the end of the verse refers back to its beginning: "Do not take," and if you have taken, return [it]. But He did not warn his son.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:4:1.hebrew: בדין הוא כו' - כרבי יוחנן, דהאי וחי אחיך לכדר"ע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:4:1.english: By right, etc. - [This accords with] Rabbi Yochanan, for this [verse], "that your brother may live [with you]," [is needed] for that [teaching] of Rabbi Akiva.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:4:2.hebrew: המסוים - שניכר שהוא גזל, ואביהם נזכר בה לקלון:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:4:2.english: Defined - [Meaning] that it is recognizable that it is stolen [property], and their father is remembered through it in disgrace.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:6:1.hebrew: דר' פנחס - בסוף חומר בקודש (חגיגה דף כו.):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:6:1.english: [That] of Rabbi Pinchas - [This is] at the end of [chapter] Chomer BaKodesh (Chagigah 26a).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:7:1.english: Do you call them robbers - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:8:1.english: They exempt the lender and the guarantor - From a negative commandment and lashes.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:8:2.english: Because they involve [a mitzvah to] arise and act - And it is [thus] a negative commandment linked to a positive commandment.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:8:3.hebrew: קומו אהדורו - מה שגביתם, וזהו נתקו לעשה, כדאמרינן: אל תקח, ואם לקחת — החזר, "וחי אחיך":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:8:3.english: Arise, return [it] - [Return] what you have collected; and this is [a prohibition] transformed into a positive commandment, as we say: "Do not take [interest], and if you took [it], return [it]," [as it is written,] "and your brother shall live [with you]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:9:1.hebrew: לאו בני אהדורי נינהו - וחי אחיך לכדר"ע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:9:1.english: They are not subject to repayment - [I.e., he expounds] "and your brother shall live" according to [the teaching of] Rabbi Akiva.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:9:2.hebrew: לא - לעולם אימא לך, אם גבה — דברי הכל אינו מתוקן בחזרה מן המלקות, דאין כאן ניתק לעשה. והאי דתני פטורין — בשלא גבו, דהתם לא הואי אלא שומא בעלמא, ששמו עליו נשך על ידי תנאי. ואתו רבי נחמיה ור' אלעזר למימר, ד״לא תשימון עליו נשך״ דקאמר רחמנא — לאו אשומא גרידתא קפיד, אלא אשומא הבא לידי גיבוי. וכל כמה שלא גבו — איכא קום עשה לקרועי שטרא. והשתא קפריך ואזיל לפרושי שינויא, ״מאי קסבר״ כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 62a:9:2.english: No - Still, I can say to you [that] if he [already] collected [the interest], all agree [that] he is not rectified from lashes by returning [it], for there is no [prohibition] linked to a positive commandment here. And that which [the baraita] teaches, "they are exempt," [refers to a case] where they have not [yet] collected [it], for there, there was only a mere assessment, in that they imposed interest upon him by means of a stipulation. And Rabbi Nechemyah and R. Elazar come to say that "you shall not impose interest upon him" [Exodus 22:24], which the Merciful One states, is not particular about a mere assessment, rather about an assessment that comes to collection. And as long as they have not collected [it], there is a [mitzvah of] "arise and do" to tear up the promissory note. And now [the Gemara] goes on to challenge [this] in order to explain the answer: "What does he hold," etc.:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 62a:14:1.hebrew: אינהו בתורת פקדון אתא לידיה - דאמר (לקמן בבא מציעא דף סג:): "מי קדחו חטין באכלבאי?" — כמו כן הייתי שומרם בבית ומוכרם ביוקר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 62a:14:1.english: [For] them, it came into his possession with the status of a deposit - For [the lender] says (below, Bava Metzia 63b): "Would the wheat have spoiled in my storage bin?" — [rather,] just the same, I would have kept them in [my] house and sold them at a high price.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 62a:6:1.hebrew: אי עשה תשובה מאי בעי גביה - למ"ד רבית קצוצה יוצאה בדיינין פריך שפיר, דהיה לו להחזיר. ואפילו למאן דאמר אינה יוצאה, מ"מ הוה לו להחזיר משום לעז ובושת; וכיון דלא חשש, גם בניו אין להם לחוש לכבודו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 62a:6:1.english: If he repented, what is [it] doing in his [possession]? - According to the one who says [that] fixed interest is recovered through the judges, [the Gemara] asks well, for he should have returned [it]. And even according to the one who says [that] it is not recovered, nevertheless he should have returned [it] because of slander and shame; and since he was not concerned [about this], his children too do not need to be concerned for his honor.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 62a:7:1.hebrew: גזלן מאי אע"פ שגבו איכא - וא"ת: דאף על פי שגבו, משום מלוה ברבית נקטי'? וי"ל: דא"כ, גזלנין למאי תננהו? פשיטא דמחזיר! להכי איצטריך ליה לשנויי: הגזלנין, מאי ניהו? מלוי ברבית:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 62a:7:1.english: "In the case of a robber, what [case of] 'even though they collected' is there?" - And if you ask: [Perhaps] it stated "even though they collected" because of the lender with interest? One can answer: If so, why did it teach "robbers"? It is obvious that [a robber] must return [what he stole]! Therefore, it was necessary for [the Gemara] to answer: "Robbers; who are they? Those who lend with interest."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 62a:8:1.hebrew: תנאי היא - וא"ת דבהגוזל (ב"ק דף צד:) משני דמחזירין לצאת ידי שמים, ואמאי לא משני נמי הכא הכי? והתם נמי, אמאי לא משני "תנאי היא" כדמשני הכא? וי"ל דהכא קאמר אליבא דר' יוחנן, ולדידיה דאמר אינה יוצאה בדיינין — אף לצאת ידי שמים אינו צריך להחזיר, ולכך לא מצי לשנויי הכא אלא "תנאי היא". וסוגיא דהתם אתי כההוא תנא דאית ליה יוצאה בדיינין, דפריך אההיא ברייתא דסברה דמן התורה מחזירין אלא משום מעשה שהיה תקנו דאין מחזירין, ופריך מהך ברייתא דהויא לאחר התקנה. ותנאי דהכא נחלקו אם יוצאה בדיינין מן התורה, ודלא כפי' ריב"ן דפירש לעיל: "למורא ניתן" — שיש לו להחזיר מיראת שמים, ולא להשבון על פי בית דין:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 62a:8:1.english: It is [a dispute between] tanna'im - And if you ask: In [the chapter] HaGozel (Bava Kamma 94b), [the Gemara] answers that they must return [it] in order to fulfill their duty to Heaven — why does [the Gemara] not answer similarly here as well? And there too, why does it not answer "It is [a dispute between] tanna'im," as it answers here? And one can answer that here [the Gemara] is speaking according to Rabbi Yochanan, and according to him who says that it is not recoverable through the judges — even to fulfill one's duty to Heaven one is not required to return [it]; therefore, here [the Gemara] could only answer "It is [a dispute between] tanna'im." And the sugya there follows that tanna who holds that it is recoverable through the judges, as [the Gemara there] raises an objection against that baraita which holds that by Torah law they must return [it], except that because of an incident that occurred, [the Sages] instituted that they do not return [it], and [the Gemara] objects from this baraita [here], which was [taught] after the enactment. And the tanna'im here dispute whether it is recoverable through the judges by Torah law — unlike the explanation of Rivan, who explained above: "It is given over to fear [of Heaven]" — meaning that one must return [it] out of fear of Heaven, and not for restitution by order of the court.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 62a:9:1.hebrew: לא מאי קום עשה לקרועי שטרא - פרש"י: וכולהו סבירא להו כוותיה דר' יוחנן, דאי גבו אין מחזירין, דתו ליכא קום עשה לאהדורי רבית, ופלוגתייהו בלא גבו. וקשה, דמעיקרא פריך אדר' יוחנן, ומשני: "תנאי היא", ופלוגתייהו ברבי יוחנן; ודחי דכולהו סבירא להו כוותיה — כל שכן דאמר ליה שפיר טפי! וי"ל דמעיקרא ודאי סבר דפליגי בלאו ד"ואל תקח מאתו נשך", ופליגי ברבי יוחנן ורבי אלעזר. ומסיק דכולהו אית להו דר' אלעזר, ולא לקי אלאו ד"אל תקח" משום דניתק לעשה הוא בהשבה; אבל פליגי בלאו ד"לא תשימון", והיכא דלא גבה עדיין הרבית: דת"ק סבר מיד כשנכתב השטר נגמרה השומא, והוי כאילו גבה כבר, ואין עוד תקנה לתקן הלאו ד"לא תשימון"; ור' נחמיה ורבי אלעזר [ב"י] סברי לאו דשומא מתלא תלי וקאי, שאם יקרע השטר קודם שיגבה — פטור. והמקשה לא הבין יפה טעמו, ופריך: "אי כגבוי דמי כו', ואי לאו כגבוי דמי, אמאי חייב לרבנן?". ומשני: "לאו כגבוי דמי", וטעמייהו דרבנן דסברי משעת כתיבה נגמרה השומא. וא"ת: והיכי ס"ד מעיקרא דפליגי ב"אל תקח"? הא אמרינן לקמן (בבא מציעא דף עה:) דערב אינו עובר אלא משום "לא תשימון" בלבד! וי"ל דהיינו כשהערב לא קבל רבית מן הלוה, אבל הכא שהערב קבל רבית מן הלוה ונתנו למלוה — לכך חייב גם משום "אל תקח" לת"ק. ואם תאמר: ואמאי לא דחי דכולהו סבירא להו כר' אלעזר, ופליגי אי חייב על לאו הניתק לעשה אי לאו? וי"ל (דהכא) הלכה דפטור, ועוד דבריש תמורה (דף ד:) פי' דלכ"ע פטור:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 62a:9:1.english: No, what is [the mitzvah to] "arise and take action"? To tear up the note - Rashi explained: All of them hold like Rabbi Yochanan, that if they collected [the interest], they do not return [it], for there is no longer [any mitzvah to] "arise and take action" to return interest, and their dispute is where they have not collected [it]. And this is difficult! For initially [the Gemara] raises an objection against Rabbi Yochanan, and answers, "It is a dispute of Tannaim," [meaning] their dispute is regarding Rabbi Yochanan['s view]; and [then] it rejects [that] and says that all of them hold like him — all the more so it said [it] to him even better! And one can answer that initially [the Gemara] certainly thought that they disagree regarding the negative commandment of "Do not take interest from him," and they disagree about [the dispute between] Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar. And it concludes that all of them hold like Rabbi Elazar, and one does not receive lashes for the negative commandment of "Do not take" because it is transformed into a positive commandment through returning [the interest]; rather, they disagree regarding the negative commandment of "You shall not place [interest upon him]," and [specifically] where he has not yet collected the interest: for the Tanna Kamma holds that immediately when the note is written, the appraisal is completed, and it is as if he has already collected [it], and there is no longer any remedy to rectify the negative commandment of "You shall not place"; whereas Rabbi Nechemyah and Rabbi Elazar [ben Yaakov] hold that the negative commandment of appraisal remains suspended, such that if he tears up the note before he collects, he is exempt. And the questioner did not understand his reasoning well, and asked: "If it is considered as collected, etc., and if it is not considered as collected, why is he liable according to the Rabbis?" And [the Gemara] answers: "It is not considered as collected," and the reasoning of the Rabbis [is] that they hold that from the time of writing, the appraisal is completed. And if you ask: How could it have entered our mind initially that they disagree about "Do not take"? Surely we say later (Bava Metzia 75b) that a guarantor only transgresses on account of "You shall not place" alone! And one can answer that that is when the guarantor did not receive interest from the borrower; but here, where the guarantor received interest from the borrower and gave it to the lender, therefore he is also liable on account of "Do not take" according to the Tanna Kamma. And if you ask: Why did [the Gemara] not reject [the inference] by saying that all of them hold like Rabbi Elazar, and they disagree whether one is liable for a negative commandment transformed into a positive commandment or not? And one can answer that (here) the halakha is that he is exempt; and furthermore, at the beginning of Temurah (4b), it is explained that according to everyone he is exempt.
